title: Hans Gugelot, Kodak Carousel S slide projector, 1963
lede: Hans Gugelot’s redesign of the Kodak round-tray projector for Europe: a square grey box under a clear-lidded slide ring, with small black controls.
summary: A square grey housing, a black numbered slide ring under a clear lid, and black lens and knobs. Gugelot for Kodak AG, 1963.

creator.name: Hans Gugelot (form design); Kodak AG, Stuttgart

evidence.note: Inspected the HfG-Archiv image of object HfG-Ar MS 0156 at 960 × 669 px through museum-digital. The case of this copy reads “Kodak Carousel S-AV”, a variant of the S. A second photograph, of a “Carousel S” on the Die Neue Sammlung website (1800 × 1371 px), shows the same form. Its object number could not be read, because the page loads its text by script.

styles.note: An Ulm-made industrial design for a non-Braun client: a plain grey box, numbered ring, and controls reduced to a few black parts.

context: The HfG-Archiv record credits Kodak AG (Stuttgart) with the manufacture and Hans Gugelot (1920–1965) with the form design, both 1963, and gives metal and electronics, 26 × 26 cm, 15 cm high. [museum-digital 2088570](https://global.museum-digital.org/object/2088570).

The record says that in the early 1960s Kodak Germany commissioned Gugelot’s “institut für produktgestaltung und design e.V.” in Neu-Ulm to redesign the round-tray projector for Europe. Gugelot bevelled the tray edge so that slides were easier to take out, and added a Plexiglas lid against dust. [museum-digital](https://global.museum-digital.org/object/2088570).
observed: The body is a square, matte grey box with slightly rounded vertical edges and a thin seam around its middle.
A round black slide tray sits on top, edged with a ring of small white numerals, under a clear flat lid.
The lens, a slide slot, and a knurled knob are black. A small vent of vertical slots sits on one side.
The name “Kodak Carousel S-AV” is printed small in white on the grey side, with “Kodak” in bold.
interpretation: The projector shows the Ulm method outside Braun: a technical object made calm by one grey volume, one radius, and small black controls.
borrow: Put a numbered scale around a circular control, in small white figures on black.

rights.statement: The museum-digital record marks the image “RR-P” (rights reserved). Photograph by Ernst Fesseler for Museum Ulm/HfG-Archiv. Gugelot died in 1965, so the design is protected in Germany until the end of 2035. No image is stored.
